objective: Take up backlog B39, given the go-ahead by the coordinator on 2026-11-10 (G1 with G5): find a ring rule and contact law with an invertible one-step map and persistent contacts on a tube, so that every row is open and growth while running could be read natively, or show that none exists; and say whether the lapse of knots under growth while running is rule 60's forgetting or growth itself. Proved where stated, computed where marked.
status: Complete 2026-11-10 (backlog B39): proved that on a finite network an injective step has finite order, at which every contact holds only its own first value, so no contact persists; hence in any finite network with a persistent contact no row after the first is open, and no finite substrate has both an invertible step and a persistent contact (checked on 256 linear substrates, first and second order, on five tubes). Reconciled with DOUBLE-BALANCE-20261109-001A: its invertible map is the own cells' evolution, not the step. Recommendation Research directions (B55 and B64).
stop_rule: Stop at a substrate with an invertible step and persistent contacts, with growth while running read on it, or at a proof that no finite substrate has both.
title: Growth on an invertible substrate
